queries: WITH r AS (SELECT link_to_event, SUM(spent) * 1.0 / SUM(amount) AS ratio FROM budget WHERE link_to_event IS NOT NULL AND spent IS NOT NULL AND amount IS NOT NULL GROUP BY link_to_event), a AS (SELECT AVG(ratio) AS avg_ratio FROM r) SELECT r.link_to_event AS event_id, r.ratio AS spend_ratio, r.ratio / a.avg_ratio AS relative_ratio FROM r CROSS JOIN a ORDER BY (r.ratio / a.avg_ratio) IS NULL, r.ratio / a.avg_ratio DESC LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: An event's spend ratio is SUM(spent)/SUM(amount) over its budget lines. Only lines where both spent and amount are non-null count. Events with no such lines are left out.
The 'average spend ratio across all events' is the simple mean of the per-event ratios, so each event counts equally. It is not the pooled total spent divided by total amount.
An event whose summed amount is 0 gets a NULL ratio, because SQLite returns NULL for division by zero. Those events sort last, and AVG skips them.

alternatives.interpretation: The average spend ratio is the pooled ratio across all budget lines (total spent / total amount), not the mean of the per-event ratios.

The 'average spend ratio across all events' is the unweighted mean of the per-event ratios, ignoring events with a NULL ratio.
